incidents.name: Zeabur infrastructure breach
incidents.summary: Zeabur says compromised internal credentials gave an attacker access to shared clusters, some dedicated servers and stored environment variables. It published an incident report and announced that the service is shutting down.
incidents.dateLabel: Attack ran Oct 14-15, 2026 (UTC); status incident opened Oct 15; shutdown announced Oct 17; preliminary report Oct 19; full wind-down Dec 1-31, 2026

sources.label: Zeabur is shutting down: what happens next

incidents.correction: The October incident followed an earlier breach. See the vendor status page and shutdown announcement for the current service position.

incidents.name: OVHcloud CLI releases backdoored
incidents.summary: OVHcloud says an attacker replaced official CLI release binaries with credential-stealing malware. Versions 0.11.0–0.15.0 were affected during a roughly 94-minute window on 19 October; 0.16.0 was not.

sources.label: The Hacker News: Hackers Hijack Five OVHcloud CLI Releases

incidents.name: Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 malware
incidents.summary: The official Rank Math PRO 3.0.123 download contained malware during an 11-hour window on 15–16 October. The vendor released clean version 3.0.124 and published recovery guidance. The free WordPress plugin was not affected.
incidents.dateLabel: Malicious download window Oct 15 20:02 UTC - Oct 16 07:12 UTC, 2026; vendor advisory Oct 16

sources.label: SecurityWeek: Rank Math PRO Compromised in Supply Chain Attack
The Hacker News: Rank Math PRO Hijacked

incidents.correction: Affects PRO 3.0.123 only, in an ~11 hour window; clean 3.0.124 already shipped.

incidents.name: TeamUpdraft customer database compromised
incidents.summary: TeamUpdraft confirmed unauthorised access over 17–18 October. It believes its customer database was accessed and says attackers abused UpdraftCentral connections to create admin accounts and install malicious plugins. The full extent is unknown. Connection keys were revoked; the plugin downloads themselves were not affected.

sources.label: TeamUpdraft: security incident - what customers need to know

incidents.correction: The vendor believes the customer database was accessed. It confirmed abuse of UpdraftCentral connections, but the extent of affected customer sites remained unknown. Its advisory was still being updated.

incidents.name: ConnectWise Cloud Backup identities compromised
incidents.summary: ConnectWise disclosed compromised application credentials used to attempt unauthorised access through Cloud Backup integrations. Microsoft later attributed the activity to Storm-0940 using ARTEX. Impact varies by tenant; a successful sign-in is not proof of data theft.
incidents.dateLabel: Discovered Oct 14; disclosed Oct 16; identities disabled Oct 17, 2026

sources.label: The Hacker News: ConnectWise Suspends Cloud Backup

incidents.correction: Microsoft’s Storm-0940 / ARTEX report below describes attribution and AI use in this same attack, not a second incident.

incidents.name: AOMEI update infrastructure hijacked
incidents.summary: Google’s threat researchers found brief tampering with AOMEI Backupper update infrastructure that redirected selected users to malware. The attacks happened between April and July; the research was published in October.
incidents.correction: Framing fix: the hijacking happened April-July 2026; only the disclosure is new this month. Vendor had not proactively notified customers as of Oct 20.

incidents.name: SubQuery npm package backdoored
incidents.summary: The @subql/common 5.8.3 npm release contained a credential-stealing payload, according to a public security report and maintainer response. It was published through the project’s release pipeline with npm provenance; provenance alone did not make it safe.
incidents.dateLabel: Malicious publish Oct 5, 2026 11:56 UTC; pulled within ~50 minutes

sources.label: GMO Flatt Security: Supply Chain Attack on @subql/common

incidents.name: Tensorlake npm credential-stealing worm
incidents.summary: tensorlake@0.5.144 was published to npm on Oct 8, 2026 carrying a Shai-Hulud-style credential-stealing worm with a destructive dead-man's switch ('hostage token'). The Register framed it as the Shai-Hulud worm's jump into AI infrastructure.
incidents.dateLabel: Malicious publish and vendor advisory Oct 8, 2026

sources.label: The Hacker News: Tensorlake npm Package Compromised

incidents.name: GhostAction GitHub workflow campaign
incidents.summary: GitGuardian reports a renewed GhostAction campaign using malicious GitHub Actions workflows to steal secrets. The 2026 targeting followed an earlier 2025 wave; targeted repositories and successful compromises are different figures.
incidents.dateLabel: Original wave Sept 2025; resurgence Aug 31-Sep 30, 2026; 30k+ repo burst Oct 8-12, 2026

sources.label: GitGuardian: GhostAction Returns (772 repos, 30k more in Oct)

incidents.correction: The 2025 and 2026 reports describe waves of the same campaign. Repository targeting figures do not equal successful compromises. See GitGuardian’s report for the effect of GitHub’s workflow blocking.

incidents.name: Plex Media Server flaws exploited (Plex2Shell)
incidents.summary: Plex confirms active exploitation of a chain of server vulnerabilities that can let an unauthenticated attacker run code. Update to 1.43.3.10861 or newer; Plex says an older internet-reachable server may already be compromised. CISA lists the four related CVEs as known exploited.
incidents.dateLabel: Exploit chain weaponized within hours of disclosure (~Oct 19); CISA KEV Oct 20, 2026

sources.label: CISA: Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

detail.whatHappened: Four Plex Media Server bugs (CVE-2026-96652, -96654, -96655, -96656) can be chained to steal an admin token and run code. Plex patched in 1.43.3 (the Sept 1 forum post). The researcher published details Oct 16 and a proof of concept three days later. Exploitation reports began Oct 17, first against honeypots to install a cryptominer. CISA added all four to KEV on Oct 20.
detail.exposure: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861. Chaining the bugs can let an unauthenticated remote attacker run code with the privileges of the Plex server process. Individual flaw scores differ; a chain score is not each individual CVE's score.
detail.fix: Update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3.10861 or newer. NAS installs may need a manual package install. Plex says an older server reachable from the internet should be treated as potentially compromised: update and follow its incident-response steps, not only apply the patch.
detail.remaining: Servers not updated since August. How many real servers are compromised is unknown.

responses.summary: Forum notice, update posted Oct 19 with CVE details and confirmation of active exploitation.
Added the four CVEs to KEV Oct 20.

claimChecks.explanation: CISA KEV listing is based on evidence of active exploitation; BleepingComputer reports cryptominer deployment, first against honeypots.
KEV data shows due date 2026-10-23 for CVE-2026-96656 and -96654, but 2026-11-03 for -96652 and -96655. The deadline binds US federal civilian agencies only.
No source says attacks are happening 'live' right now beyond the reported campaign since Oct 17.

incidents.name: SafePay ransomware advisory
incidents.summary: A new CISA/FBI advisory describes SafePay ransomware activity and at least 600 victims across critical infrastructure sectors. The advisory is new, not the group: SafePay has operated since 2024.
incidents.dateLabel: Joint advisory published Oct 20-21, 2026; group active since Aug 2024

sources.label: CISA news release: CISA, FBI and partners warn of SafePay actors

incidents.correction: Not a new campaign: the advisory is new this week but SafePay has operated since Aug 2024. The advisory itself states the actors impacted at least 600 separate victims across multiple critical infrastructure sectors - the 'hundreds of organizations' framing is supported.

incidents.name: Palo Alto firewalls targeted by ransomware groups
incidents.summary: Reporting links multiple ransomware groups to exploitation of a patched PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass. The attacks began months before this week’s reporting; this is not a newly discovered October intrusion.
incidents.correction: Framing fix: onset was May 2026, not this week; this month's news is expanded/continued ransomware exploitation of the same patched CVE.

incidents.name: Tor exit relays hijacked
incidents.summary: A researcher found 333 Tor exit relays (~10% of the network's ~3,000 exits) redirecting SSH connections through 12 interception servers using the Ebury OpenSSH backdoor, harvesting passwords when users accepted forged host keys. Exit policies on hundreds of relays were rewritten Oct 1-5; Tor directory authorities removed the compromised relays around Oct 20-21.
incidents.dateLabel: Exit-policy rewrites Oct 1-5; researcher scan Oct 2; removals and coverage Oct 20-22, 2026
incidents.correction: The figure of 333 exit relays comes from a researcher’s scan. It is a reported observation, not an independently verified count of distinct breached relay operators.

incidents.name: TiDB Cloud (PingCAP) breach
incidents.summary: PingCAP confirms unauthorised access to internal cloud resources between 9 September and 7 October, including copied data and source code. The breach is confirmed, but claims about plaintext keys and the full customer impact are disputed or unresolved.

sources.label: PingCAP: Customer Actions - October 2026 Security Incident

incidents.correction: Breach confirmed; scope disputed - attacker leak-site figures (10.6 TB, 115k plaintext keys) are unverified claims that conflict with PingCAP's statement that keys were encrypted and unused.

incidents.name: SBI customer data on dark web
incidents.summary: SBI told stock exchanges that customer records had surfaced on the dark web, according to reporting. Reports distinguish more than 375,000 records from 3,897 containing personal information. The bank was still assessing authenticity and scope.
incidents.dateLabel: Bank alerted Oct 16; exchange filing and coverage Oct 21, 2026

sources.label: The Hindu: SBI admits exposure of customer data on the Dark Web
Moneycontrol: SBI flags data leak, says no material impact
Indian Express: SBI data leak explained

incidents.correction: Reporting distinguishes more than 375,000 records from 3,897 containing personal information. Authenticity and scope remained under assessment; neither figure establishes that every record belongs to a different person.

detail.whatHappened: State Bank of India told stock exchanges on Oct 21, 2026 that about 375,000 records tied to it were found on the dark web, and that its preliminary analysis found 3,897 records with personal information. It learned of it on Oct 16 from its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In.
detail.exposure: For the 3,897: names, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, gender, emails, addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs and loan/lead metadata. The bank says authenticity and completeness still need a detailed investigation and that core operations are not affected.
detail.fix: SBI activated incident response and hired a CERT-In-empanelled agency. Customers have not been given specific steps in the checked sources.
detail.remaining: Source of the leak, authenticity and full scope are not established. The Internet Freedom Foundation says affected customers could get calls from people posing as SBI who can recite their details, and wants SBI to notify them (The Hindu). BusinessToday says a group called Siriusim had claimed the hack on BreachForums; that claim is not verified.

responses.by: SBI, as quoted by The Hindu
responses.summary: Exchange disclosure with 3,897 PII records, investigation under way, no material business impact.

claimChecks.claim: SBI CONFIRMED 3,897 customers' mobile, DOB, address + loan data on dark web
claimChecks.explanation: SBI itself disclosed 3,897 PII records among ~375,000 found, per preliminary analysis, including loan/lead metadata. 'Confirmed' overstates it: the bank says authenticity and completeness are still being established. Say 'SBI disclosed'.

incidents.name: Siemens Software Center flaw exploited
incidents.summary: Attackers are abusing a DLL side-loading flaw in the signed Siemens Software Center client through ClickFix lures. Siemens says its systems and update channel were not breached.
incidents.dateLabel: Advisory SSA-580366 Oct 15; Siemens validated active exploitation Oct 19; CISA KEV Oct 20, 2026

sources.label: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Siemens advisory AV26-1063

incidents.correction: Not a breach of Siemens infrastructure: attackers abuse the signed client via ClickFix lures. Siemens explicitly states no Siemens system or update channel was breached.

incidents.name: North Korea state-sponsored activity (multiple October items)
incidents.summary: The original list does not identify which North Korea-linked campaign it means. Reporting on Operation FlashHole is one possible lead, not a confirmed match to that claim.
incidents.dateLabel: Original claim not tied to a specific campaign

sources.label: IC3 PSA: North Korean IT Workers Expanding Use of Facilitators
The Record: North Korean hackers target Ukrainian experts

incidents.correction: The unspecific North Korea claim cannot be assigned to one event. October reporting covers separate campaigns and enforcement actions. Linked reports are leads, not evidence that they are the same campaign.

incidents.name: eMudhra / weak certificate keys
incidents.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate certificate-authority keys were weak enough to recover from public certificates, including one with the value 4. eMudhra revoked them. Its account says none issued end-entity certificates; this is not a confirmed breach of its infrastructure.
incidents.dateLabel: Reported 17–18 Oct; revoked 19 Oct; public 20–21 Oct 2026

sources.label: eMudhra official statement (3 updates · Original source
Google: Protecting Chrome and Android users
The Register: eMudhra defends its keys

incidents.correction: The vendor describes weak-key revocation rather than an infrastructure breach. Tailscale and Node.js updates are downstream responses, not additional breaches. Detailed timing and scope are in the vendor statement and Cloudflare report.

detail.whatHappened: In April 2025 eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, ran a key ceremony that produced eight intermediate CA certificates with badly weak private keys. A researcher found they could be recovered from the public certificates (some keys were single or double digit numbers, one reportedly just 4). He reported it to Mozilla, Chrome, Apple and Microsoft on Oct 17, 2026. eMudhra revoked all eight on Oct 19.
detail.exposure: Anyone who worked out the keys could have forged a trusted certificate for any website, but only against software that does not check Certificate Transparency or revocation lists. Chrome and Google say no certificates chaining to these intermediates had been logged to CT, so CT-enforcing browsers could not have been attacked. No exploitation has been shown. The 'eight keys' were six TLS intermediates and two code-signing intermediates.
detail.fix: Mozilla blocked them via OneCRL on Oct 17 (done for standard Firefox users by 22:59 UTC) and shipped Firefox 158.0.1, ESR 115.43.1 and 153.5.1, plus NSS 3.131.1 removing the signing root. Chrome blocked them by CRLSet the same day, and removed the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from its root store. The reporter also says Apple and Microsoft blocked the certificates; their exact update dates were not independently verified here. Cloudflare, Node.js and Tailscale shipped updates.
detail.remaining: Software that ships its own trust store or ignores revocation needs updates. eMudhra has not confirmed a root cause; it says a wrap/unwrap step created a second weak key set. It says seven of the eight were never used and the eighth issued no certificates. It says one US customer ecosystem needs replacement certificates. Investigation ongoing; MeitY has set up a probe panel.

responses.summary: Says keys were revoked, no certificates issued from them, no data breached, signing/eSign services unaffected, key ceremony flaw not yet fully explained. Offers backup CA to enterprise TLS customers.
Received report Oct 17 20:06 UTC, blocked within hours, shipped Firefox and NSS updates.
Blocked by CRLSet Oct 17, removed the signing root from Chrome Root Store, says CT-enforcing clients were not exposed.
Patched WARP, cloudflared, CDN and Zero Trust; found no active exploitation on its services; lists customer actions.
Lists the eight intermediates with hashes and notes eMudhra stopped issuing under its G3 root.

claimChecks.explanation: The Register says one was just the number 4 and others were two or three digit numbers. Talos says several keys evaluated to single or double digit integers. Mozilla's bug (2083449) is the underlying report.

Eight intermediates had recoverable keys, so forging any site was possible in principle. No forged certificate or attack has been shown. Google says no certificates were logged to CT, so CT-enforcing browsers were not exposed. Say 'could have', not 'forged'.
Intermediates created Apr 30, 2025, reported Oct 17, 2026, about 17.5 months of vulnerability. eMudhra says about 18 months. Window of weakness, not of known abuse.

60 million is how many certificates eMudhra says it has issued overall (The Register's framing). The compromised intermediates reportedly issued none, and eMudhra says the impact is one US customer ecosystem. Do not state 60M at risk.

incidents.name: Railway / possible secret exposure
incidents.summary: Railway says an unauthorised party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and decrypted some of them. It paused deployments during its investigation and recommended credential rotation. The affected-account scope remained unresolved.

sources.label: Railway Status: Platform Outage incident QH8L8B3E

incidents.correction: Railway confirmed the investigation, not a final count of exposed accounts. The deployment pause was precautionary. Follow the current status page for restoration updates.

incidents.name: LiteLLM / backdoored releases
incidents.summary: LiteLLM confirms its release pipeline pushed malicious 1.107.0 packages to PyPI and container registries. The malware stole credentials and loaded remote-code tools. Affected artifacts were removed; private enterprise releases were not impacted.
incidents.correction: This is the October 1.107.0 compromise, separate from the earlier 2026 1.82.x incident. The official advisory lists affected registry tags and the exposure windows.

incidents.name: OpenCode / exposed provider keys
incidents.summary: OpenCode confirmed a security breach affecting 1.4% of Console users during a large-scale attack. Reporting says stored keys for linked AI providers were exposed and some users saw unauthorised charges. The official post confirms the breach, not an audited total of financial losses.
incidents.dateLabel: Exposure reported from 17 Oct 2026; press 19 Oct
incidents.correction: The official OpenCode statement is linked alongside reporting and maintainer commentary. The company described a distillation attack; user charges and wider attribution are not independently audited. Do not treat every linked comment as a confirmed technical finding.

incidents.name: PHP / PHP2Shell
incidents.summary: PHP fixed two critical core bugs, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The PHP team rates both 9.2 and urges immediate updates. All web-serving PHP installations need review, with the highest demonstrated risk in Apache mod_php.

sources.label: JFrog Security Research: PHP2Shell - all you need to know

incidents.correction: This is a vulnerability and patch advisory, not proof that every PHP installation was breached. CISA advises taking systems offline if they cannot be patched or run PHP 8.1 or older; it does not tell every patched site to go offline.

detail.whatHappened: Two memory-handling bugs in PHP itself can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. One involves out-of-memory cleanup; the other leaves stale state for a later request in the same worker. PHP released fixes on Oct 21. The PHP project uses the CVE identifiers; php2shell is the researchers' name.
detail.exposure: PHP rates both CVSS v4.0 9.2 (the leaked post claimed 10.0). On Apache mod_php, an unauthenticated request can trigger the first bug before application code runs. Amazon Threat Intelligence (via Tenable) reports exploitation attempts from Oct 17, before disclosure. CISA's Oct 21 alert said it had not itself observed exploitation at publication.
detail.fix: Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. CISA says take PHP systems offline if you cannot patch or you run PHP 8.1 or older, and that a WAF may give partial protection.
detail.remaining: PHP is embedded in many products, so inventory is hard. End-of-life branches have no official fix except source backports (per Tenable). The PHP Foundation admitted a fix for the underlying out-of-memory problem had stalled for months.

responses.summary: Urges immediate patching; offline if unpatchable or PHP 8.1 and older.
Explains the bugs, credits finders, admits the fix was delayed by decision-making and resources.
Timeline of the leak and IPS/WAF coverage.

claimChecks.explanation: PHP and Check Point both give CVSS v4.0 9.2 and unauthenticated RCE.
W3Techs on Oct 22 says PHP is used by 69.3% of sites whose server-side language is known. Not 70% of all websites.

CISA says patch immediately; take systems offline only if you cannot update or run PHP 8.1 or earlier. WordPress, Drupal and Laravel are affected only if they run an unpatched PHP; CISA's alert does not name them.
Amazon Threat Intelligence reports attempts from Oct 17 per Tenable; CISA had not observed any at its publication time. Not on the KEV list in the captured sources.

incidents.name: GitLab / critical Onigmo flaw
incidents.summary: GitLab released fixes for CVE-2026-110264, a CVSS 10.0 flaw in its bundled regular-expression compiler that could allow unauthenticated code execution under certain conditions. Older self-managed releases are affected; no exploitation was known in the captured reporting.

sources.label: GitLab Critical Patch Release · Original source
TrustList: GitLab ships another CVSS 10 regex fix

incidents.correction: Potential remote code execution is not proof of exploitation. The advisory concerns self-managed GitLab; hosted services and detailed supported release guidance are covered in GitLab’s own notice.

detail.whatHappened: On Oct 21, 2026 GitLab shipped a critical patch for CVE-2026-110264, an integer overflow in its regular expression compiler. Under certain conditions it could let an unauthenticated user run code on a self-managed server. GitLab rates it CVSS 10.0; the detailed exploitation conditions are not public.
detail.exposure: Self-managed GitLab CE and EE only. GitLab lists affected versions from 7.0 up to the fixed releases. An Oct 12 fix for a different bug does not resolve this Oct 21 vulnerability. GitLab.com already runs the fixed version. Same release also fixes high-severity LDAP auto-linking and OAuth/OIDC cache poisoning issues.
detail.remaining: No reported exploitation and not on CISA KEV as of Oct 22 per The Hacker News. Exploitation conditions undisclosed.

responses.summary: Critical patch release; strongly recommends all self-managed installs upgrade immediately.

claimChecks.explanation: GitLab's own current patch notice lists CVSS 10.0 and affected releases from 7.0, and says an unauthenticated user could execute code under certain conditions. That is not proof every server was exploited.
CVE-2026-97229 (Oct 12) and CVE-2026-110264 (Oct 21) are different. Use the Oct 21 one for the current claim.

incidents.name: NGINX / five medium-severity advisories
incidents.summary: NGINX’s October release fixed five newly published security advisories. The vendor rates all five medium, not critical. One concerns HTTP/3; this is distinct from the separate Header Accordions research.

sources.label: nginx CHANGES (1.31.7 released 14 Oct 2026, security fixes)

incidents.correction: The circulating description of “three critical vulnerabilities” does not match this release: NGINX lists five medium-severity advisories. Its HTTP/3 issue is separate from Header Accordions.

incidents.name: Cairn / AI-assisted intrusion research
incidents.summary: Norforge reports exposed dashboards showing threat actors abusing the open-source Cairn agent platform for intrusion attempts. Its researcher told press that one actor breached more than 100 companies. This is a research assessment, not a verified victim-by-victim count.
incidents.correction: Cairn is the tool being abused, not a breached vendor. The 100+ figure is attributed to the researcher. This entry omits victim names originating in excluded reporting. The separate Microsoft ARTEX campaign should not be assumed to be the same operation.

incidents.name: Signal / call hang-up flaw
incidents.summary: Reporting describes a RingRTC flaw that could let a malicious participant continue receiving audio after the other person hangs up. Camera continuation is not confirmed. The issue concerns call shutdown, not a general break of Signal encryption.
incidents.correction: Press reports describe audio continuation with a malicious call participant. Camera continuation remains uncertain. The library fix and the first fixed mobile app versions should not be assumed to be identical.

incidents.name: Tailscale / eMudhra response
incidents.summary: Tailscale published an emergency update to distrust the compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates. This is a downstream certificate-trust response, not a separate Tailscale breach. WireGuard mesh traffic does not rely on that public certificate trust.
incidents.correction: This is a follow-on to the eMudhra certificate incident, not an independent Tailscale compromise. See bulletin TS-2026-013 and the current changelog.

detail.whatHappened: Tailscale published bulletin TS-2026-013 on the eMudhra keys. Its client trusts whatever the operating system's certificate store trusts, so a forged eMudhra-signed certificate would have been accepted on devices that still trusted those intermediates.
detail.exposure: Only web PKI connections that rely on the system store. Tailscale says node-to-node WireGuard traffic does not use that store and is not affected. No exploitation reported in the bulletin.
detail.fix: Tailscale v1.104.2 or later (built with Go 1.27.3) explicitly distrusts the compromised certificates. Tailscale's own services were updated.
detail.remaining: Devices on older clients with OS stores that still contain the intermediates.

responses.summary: Bulletin TS-2026-013: update to v1.104.2 or later. Listed by Oct 21-22; a per-bulletin publication date was not visible.

claimChecks.explanation: Tailscale was not breached. It published a bulletin and a client fix as a downstream user of the OS certificate store. The bulletin page lists it without a visible per-item date in what was fetched, so keep the Oct 21 date as 'listed by Oct 21-22'.

incidents.name: Node.js / security releases
incidents.summary: Node.js shipped October security releases covering four high-severity flaws alongside medium- and low-severity fixes. The release also updates certificate trust after eMudhra. Patched vulnerabilities do not by themselves establish an intrusion.

sources.label: Node.js blog: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 Security Releases

incidents.correction: The same release includes both independent vulnerability fixes and an eMudhra certificate-trust update. They are not all caused by the certificate incident.

detail.whatHappened: On Oct 21, 2026 the Node.js project shipped security releases v22.23.4, v24.22.1 and v26.12.1 fixing ten CVEs and updating bundled c-ares, OpenSSL (24.x, 22.x), SQLite (22.x), Undici and the CA certificate list to drop the eMudhra intermediates.
detail.exposure: CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can permit remote code execution, affects 26.x, 24.x and 22.x. The release also fixes TLS hostname bypasses (CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069), a dns.resolve NUL truncation (CVE-2026-105482) and others. Node rates the highest of them 'high', not critical.
detail.fix: Upgrade to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1. End-of-life Node versions stay affected.
detail.remaining: Node's post does not say whether any of the ten CVEs was exploited. Treat that as unknown.

responses.summary: Security release across three lines; also removes eMudhra intermediates from the bundled cert list.

claimChecks.explanation: Listed as 'Node.js Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write permits remote code execution', severity high.
Two high-severity TLS hostname-validation bypasses (CVE-2026-105483, CVE-2026-106069), not one.
Ten CVEs counted on the advisory; release date Oct 21, 2026 (not Oct 22).
Advisory lists 'ca-cert (eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise)' as a dependency update.

incidents.name: California students / ETS data breach
incidents.summary: California’s education department notified families about files copied from testing contractor ETS. The records span three school years and include sensitive student information. The copying happened between May and September, not during this week’s reporting.

sources.label: California Dept. of Education · Original source

incidents.correction: The intrusion occurred months before public disclosure. ETS was the affected contractor; California’s notification describes the student-data categories and three-school-year scope.

incidents.name: HTTP/3 / Header Accordions
incidents.summary: Foxio’s research describes QPACK header-decompression amplification that can exhaust server memory. Seven of ten tested implementations were affected, with patch status varying by implementation. This is a vulnerability report, not proof that all affected servers were attacked.
incidents.correction: The affected implementation list and patch status were captured at disclosure. This is distinct from NGINX’s separately listed HTTP/3 issue. Consult the original research for current changes.

incidents.name: Onamae / Desktop Cloud compromise
incidents.summary: Onamae says malicious programs were placed in customer Desktop Cloud server environments. Up to 26,739 servers were potentially affected, and it began stopping servers to contain the incident. Data viewing was possible; data theft was not confirmed.
incidents.correction: The provider’s potentially affected server count is not a confirmed count of servers with stolen data. The incident concerns the Desktop Cloud product, not every Onamae or GMO service.

incidents.name: Ahold Delhaize / service disruption
incidents.summary: Ahold Delhaize took systems offline after detecting malicious activity, disrupting websites, apps and deliveries. Stores remained open. Its 19 October update reported recovery progress and no evidence then of sensitive data theft.
incidents.correction: The incident began on 12 October, before this week’s reporting. The company’s no-evidence-of-data-theft statement is time-bound and does not close the investigation.

incidents.name: Bullhorn / outages and incident response
incidents.summary: Bullhorn’s status updates describe separate events: a contained 17 October cyber incident, precautionary PHP2Shell product shutdowns, and a 21 October login outage linked to database-replication lag. They should not be presented as one confirmed breach.
incidents.correction: The PHP shutdown, the earlier cyber incident and login replication problems are separate. The status page is a changing source; this entry reflects the captured 21–22 October updates.

incidents.name: Medi-Cal / Paradigm contractor breach
incidents.summary: Reporting says a Paradigm Healthcare Services breach affected more than 970,000 Medi-Cal members. The intrusion was detected in October 2025; notifications followed in September 2026. This is a contractor incident, not a confirmed breach of California’s own systems.
incidents.correction: This is a 2025 intrusion with 2026 notification and reporting. The affected contractor handled Medi-Cal claims. The underlying HHS portal entry was not independently captured here.

incidents.name: Rajasthan Police data breach (claimed)
incidents.summary: A group calling itself Scarlettgroup claims to have breached Rajasthan Police and offered data for sale. Coverage repeats claims of about 70,000 identity records and 59,460 mobile numbers. These figures and the alleged breach are unverified.

detail.whatHappened: On Oct 21, coverage attributed to an X monitoring account reported that a group calling itself Scarlettgroup claimed to have breached Rajasthan Police. The group claims about 70,000 identity records and 59,460 mobile numbers, plus documents and attachments. These are the group's claims, not independently verified counts.
detail.exposure: Unknown. Nobody independent has confirmed the data is genuine, or that it came from Rajasthan Police systems. If genuine it would be an identity theft and fraud risk.
detail.remaining: Authenticity, source system and scope are all unconfirmed. Coverage reported no Rajasthan Police comment at publication. No leak forum or sample data was accessed for this index.

responses.summary: BusinessToday reported no police comment at publication on Oct 21. This is absence of a response in that coverage, not a police statement.

claimChecks.claim: Group claims 70,000 identity records + 59,460 numbers for sale. Unverified.
claimChecks.explanation: The numbers match the group's own claim as reported. Keep status 'alleged'. No confirmation by police or independent researchers found.
